greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Here's your midweek catch-up, with polling day now just days away.

lead.headline: More than 1.5 million Victorians vote early as campaign enters final days
lead.summary: The electoral commission says more than 1.5 million people had already voted by Wednesday morning, ahead of Saturday's state election. Liberal leader Jess Wilson campaigned on graffiti clean-up in Prahran, while Labor is promoting a $460 million free dental package.

stories.headline: Faster four-colouring of maps wins a FOCS best paper award
stories.summary: This peer-reviewed FOCS 2026 paper colours planar graphs with four colours in near-linear time, a big step up from older quadratic methods, and is drawing fresh press after winning Best Paper. The link is the authors' open arXiv copy; their separate linear-time follow-up is also on arXiv.

stories.headline: AI agents run a biology lab with limited human help
stories.summary: Published in Nature on 4 November, this paper presents an AI-run lab system that coordinates instruments through multi-step biology experiments, including writing and reading messages in DNA. It stands out as a test of AI agents working beyond the screen.

stories.headline: Do AI vision models really work like brains?
stories.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence paper from earlier this year, back in the news this week, tests whether brain activity can predict a model's internal features, not just the other way round. Many features did not match, suggesting that models predicting brain responses well may still work quite differently.

stories.headline: Nvidia board brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
stories.summary: Less than two weeks after Huang resigned, Nvidia's board reinstated him, saying input from senior US government levels led it to conclude his return poses no national security risk. Shares jumped about 31% on Monday before giving back some of the gain, while investigations continue.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship for AI code review and approval
stories.summary: The new bundle has AI agents review GitHub pull requests, work on fixes and decide on approvals under team policy, with two of its three parts in beta. Approval does not merge code by itself, and Anthropic warns the system can still miss bugs.

stories.headline: Former xAI founders unveil a startup that aims to predict the future
stories.summary: Three people who co-founded xAI have launched Epochal, a new company working on technology to forecast future events.

stories.headline: What the parties are offering first-home buyers
stories.summary: Labor points to more than 25,000 new homes for first-home buyers under a joint federal plan, while the Coalition would scrap stamp duty for them on homes up to $1 million. The Greens want stamp duty gone on homes under $1.1 million and a two-year rent freeze.

stories.headline: CFA volunteer in critical condition after grassfire
stories.summary: A volunteer firefighter is in an induced coma at The Alfred after a fast-moving fire at Nandaly, in the state's north-west, burned beneath the tanker they were in on Sunday. The CFA is investigating.

stories.headline: Man found not guilty of photographer's murder due to mental impairment
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the man accused of killing Dominic O'Brien in Footscray last year was psychotic at the time. He will be subject to supervision, with the orders to be decided later.

stories.headline: Russia warns Estonia it is close to triggering open war
stories.summary: Moscow's warning comes as Estonia plans to close its border crossings with Russia from 1 December, after accusing Russian services of an attempted arson attack. Russia denies that, and Estonia denies Moscow's claim that it lets Ukrainian drones use its airspace.

stories.headline: Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says the tankers caught fire despite a US military escort. Separately, the US has widened its sanctions on Iranian exchange houses, front companies and key figures.
